Details: A zombie outbreak begins from a selected profile and spreads through vulnerable regions.
Type Options: Diverse, Random, Standard, Rabid, Parasitic, Mutant, Undead, Necrotic, Demonic, Connected
Intensity Scaling: Low, Medium, High, and Maximum increase outbreak count, starting territory, spawned divisions, and early pressure.

Details: An artificial army appears across Eastern Europe and the western Soviet borderlands.
Type Options: Standard clone army or stronger Aryan variant
Intensity Scaling: Low, Medium, High, and Maximum scale territory, divisions, army experience, equipment stockpiles, and pressure on neighboring countries.

Details: The Soviet Union breaks apart as the Union Unmade crisis releases its republics.
Intensity Scaling: Low, Medium, High, and Maximum add scaled breakaway armies, manpower, infantry equipment, support equipment, artillery, and motorized equipment.

Details:
Pact: Turns eligible minor governments into dispersed Fury states and organizes them into the Fury Pact. Higher intensity spreads the pact farther across the world and strengthens its opening forces.

Hostile: Turns eligible minor governments into dispersed hostile Fury states that immediately pursue neighboring wars. Higher intensity spreads the Fury farther across the world and strengthens their opening attacks.
Type Options: Pact forms the Fury Pact among Fury states. Hostile mode sends Fury states into wars with neighbors and rival Fury governments.
Intensity Scaling:
Low: Creates two dispersed Fury actors immediately. Your country and its aligned countries remain outside the opening.

Medium: Creates five dispersed Fury actors immediately. Your country and its aligned countries remain outside the opening.

High: Creates nine dispersed Fury actors immediately. Your country and its aligned countries remain outside the opening.

Maximum: Creates up to sixteen dispersed Fury actors when enough suitable countries exist. Your country and its aligned countries remain outside the opening.

Details: Death begins with a hidden origin, extra islands, and a mainland reveal before natural growth carries the crisis further.
Intensity Scaling: Low starts with one hidden island, one mainland reveal state, and one weak passive host. Medium adds a small island pattern, one mainland reveal state, extra mainland pressure, and two weak passive hosts. High widens the island pattern, adds mainland pressure around the world, and brings two stronger hosts. Maximum opens the widest instant island pattern, multiple mainland pressure points, and four stronger hosts.

Details: A selected country enters a season of varied disasters, with warnings, damage, recovery, and follow-up risks.
Type Options: Random Barrage, Geological Crisis, Weather Crisis, Skyfall Crisis, Full Catalogue
Intensity Scaling: Low intensity starts a varied local season with ordinary warnings, affected-country reports, and recovery work. Medium intensity lengthens the sequence and opens regional damage with heavier recovery pressure. High intensity creates severe chained disasters with catastrophic impacts and emergency aftermath work. Maximum intensity can unleash rupture waves, meteor showers, massive eruptions, delayed tsunami chains, and moving storm corridors before the rescue and reconstruction struggle.

Details:
Sovereign Scatter: Every viable independence movement breaks away. Hosts keep a protected remnant, each new state gets its own starting territory, and none joins a league or faction. Intensity changes territory, forces, and pressure.

Open Congress: Every viable independence movement breaks away from a protected host. The new states join an informal congress, and higher intensity strengthens its charter and shared reserve.

Separation Wars: Every viable independence movement breaks away. A new state able to confront its former host may open one war of separation. The others receive a regional threat mission.

Host Wars: Every viable independence movement breaks away. Each new state may open one war against its former host. Hosts keep their homelands, and wars that cannot start become regional threat missions.

Neighbor Wars: Every viable independence movement breaks away. Each new state may open one war against a neighboring state released in the same crisis. Each state is targeted once, so no all-against-all cascade follows.

Outsider Wars: Every viable independence movement breaks away. Each new state may open one war against a nearby independent state outside the League and every faction. Each target is chosen once and distance keeps the crisis regional.

Patron Worlds: Every viable independence movement breaks away. Each new state seeks one reachable major patron, favoring shared ideology and regional proximity. Intensity scales influence, aid, and recognition.

Great Partition: Every viable independence movement breaks away. Each host keeps one protected remnant, preferring its capital, then a safe core state. Higher intensity adds the next tier of territory, border pressure, claims, and ambitions.
Type Options: Sovereign Scatter, Open Congress, Separation Wars, Host Wars, Neighbor Wars, Outsider Wars, Patron Worlds, Great Partition
Intensity Scaling:
Low: Each release gets only its starting territory, fragile defenses, scarce stocks, weak institutions, low recognition, and severe instability.

Medium: Releases receive compact territory, militia and border formations, baseline institutions, and ordinary route access.

High: Releases receive wider territory where borders allow, armed forces, stronger depots and officers, firmer institutions, and faster ambitions.

Maximum: Releases receive the largest territory and forces, rare support where their route allows it, high-chaos access, early formable discovery, and aggressive AI.

Details:
Random Coalition: Governments from available states form a coalition against the chosen target.

Regional Ring: Neighboring and same-continent minor governments form a regional ring around the target.

Ideological Front: Governments opposed to the target organize around a common regime-pressure campaign.

Great-Power Sponsor: A strategically placed major sponsor organizes the coalition around its support.

Unlikely Coalition: Distant or politically mismatched partners join despite conflicting promises that weaken their opening resolve.
Type Options: Regional Ring, Ideological Front, Great-Power Sponsor, Unlikely Coalition, Random Coalition
Intensity Scaling:
Low: a compact coalition of three governments enters the crisis with limited stockpiles. A great-power-backed coalition is led by one major with two minor partners. Every other formation draws all three members from minor governments.

Medium: five governments enter with established liaison and logistics. A great-power-backed coalition gives one seat to its major sponsor. Every other formation draws all five members from minor governments.

High: one major and six minor governments with coordinated logistics and advanced preparations.

Maximum: up to twelve governments and up to two major powers can join when enough suitable candidates exist, with full war pressure and challenge eligibility at the widest opening.

Details:
Discipline Collapse: A wartime supply crisis has broken discipline inside selected formations. Field Hunger rises while damaged commands attempt containment before predation spreads beyond the first theaters.

Ritual Cells: Officer circles and hidden field kitchens have become organized ritual cells. Cult Cohesion is already visible, and several countries may begin with compromised commands.

Silent Islands: Remote ports and island garrisons have fallen quiet behind broken convoy schedules. Communes begin with mature cells, exposed sea routes, and a growing risk of armed island hosts.

Warlord States: Armed host countries emerge from occupied feeding grounds. Each begins with a regional command, an origin doctrine, scavenged stores, and forces raised from the territory it has seized.

Convergence: Several mature host countries answer a common signal. A public convergence warning begins after launch, leaving the world time to destroy the likely hosts and sever their routes before a final authority emerges.
Type Options: Discipline Collapse, Ritual Cells, Silent Islands, Warlord States, Convergence
Intensity Scaling:
Low: A narrow crisis begins with limited territory and forces. Containment remains possible, but delay will strengthen the cells.

Medium: Several formations or theaters enter the crisis. Supply pressure, concealment, and foreign routes will demand an organized response.

High: Mature cells and armed hosts begin with strong cohesion, severe command damage, and multiple routes across the map.

Maximum: A broad international network begins with numerous theaters and host countries. Escalation is immediate, but its supply lines, leaders, territories, and convergence routes can still be attacked.

Details:
Africa Is One: Unites Africa under a powerful continental state, establishes the Charter League and its regional institutions, and prepares the wars required to complete unification.

World Is One: Forms Africa and prepares the World Is One final campaign. Rival continental powers become eligible for treaties, containment, or war, while the proclamation of The World still requires every continental dispute to be resolved and the final settlement ratified.
Type Options: Africa Is One, World Is One
Intensity Scaling:
Forms Africa and opens the continental systems immediately. Low intensity adds a limited emergency force and modest authority, reach, consent, and readiness.

Forms Africa and opens the continental systems immediately. Medium intensity adds a regional emergency force and stronger authority, reach, consent, and readiness.

Forms Africa and opens the continental systems immediately. High intensity adds a large emergency force and broadens the opening values.

Forms Africa and opens the continental systems immediately. Maximum intensity adds the largest emergency force and strongest opening values.

Details: A contagious Black Plague erupts across multiple continents. A Rat Nation rises among the infected while the Rat King gathers a separate royal basin. The outbreak advances through an escalating chain of plague evolutions.
Intensity Scaling:
Low intensity: Seeds three eligible continents with a limited Black Plague crisis. Establishes 14 infected states, 2 lesser brood basins, and 1 Royal Basin state. Evolutions I through IV begin active. Evolution V and world end remain locked.

Medium intensity: Seeds four eligible continents with a regional Black Plague crisis. Establishes 28 infected states, 3 lesser brood basins, and 2 Royal Basin states. Evolutions I through IV begin active. Evolution V and world end remain locked.

High intensity: Seeds five eligible continents, or all when fewer exist. Establishes 52 infected states, 4 lesser brood basins, and 4 Royal Basin states. Evolutions I through IV begin active. Evolution V and world end remain locked.

Maximum intensity: Seeds every eligible inhabited continent with a Black Plague crisis. Establishes 90 infected states, 6 lesser brood basins, and 8 Royal Basin states. The Rat Nation and Rat King emerge as separate realms. Evolution V and world end remain locked.

Details:
The Barracks Overflow: Unbidden ordinary formations and organized arsenal lots appear in great numbers. Their mutinies divide command staffs, open immediate conventional wars, and crowd supply routes without calling any anomalous host.

The Arsenal Draw: Rebel formations draw uneven packages of armor, motor transport, amphibious equipment, and other specialist materiel. Powerful machines may arrive without support, and other fronts may receive narrow military curiosities.

The Generals' Muster: Randomly composed formations rally behind claimant commanders. Every affected country faces an immediate personalized revolt or military takeover attempt.

The Impossible Host: Nonhuman formations rise under new regional commands and begin their wars immediately. Zombie, ghost, and golem hosts establish armed breakaways wherever their ranks gather.
Type Options: The Barracks Overflow, The Arsenal Draw, The Generals' Muster, The Impossible Host
Intensity Scaling:
Low intensity starts immediate revolts and regional wars. It affects a smaller share of countries able to sustain an open front and establishes one principal front in each selected command area.

Medium intensity starts immediate revolts and regional wars. It spreads several formations across broad command areas and establishes full-strength local fronts.

High intensity starts immediate revolts and regional wars. It affects many countries at once, establishes larger formations, and can open several rival fronts.

Maximum intensity starts a near-global wave of immediate revolts and regional wars. It reaches every country able to sustain an open front and establishes the largest sustainable formations and number of fronts.

Details: A murder shakes the succession of an eligible government and opens an investigation into a hidden movement. Higher intensity gives it more reach and cohesion, and later discoveries may reveal threats beyond the first killing.
Intensity Scaling:
§RStarts Assassin Network immediately.§! Low intensity opens a Murder Cult investigation with low reach and a small foreign network. No Assassin State exists at launch.

§RStarts Assassin Network immediately.§! Medium intensity opens a mature international network and a stronger investigation. The host can still prevent the Assassin State split.

§RStarts Assassin Network immediately.§! High intensity opens the Assassin State war and a strong foreign network.

§RStarts Assassin Network immediately.§! Maximum intensity opens Evolution IV, the Assassin State war, and foreign operations. World of Anarchy still needs its usual end conditions.

Details:
Global Proliferation: Establishes or expands missile programmes across eligible countries. Higher intensity grants stronger technology, larger reserves, more launch capacity, and better readiness without choosing a future crisis.

Saturation War: Turns an existing war between missile powers into an arms race. The belligerents gain larger arsenals and the ability to prepare saturation attacks, while neutral countries retain ordinary programmes.

Command Breakdown: Exposes vulnerable missile powers to guidance failures and rogue launch commands. Control may weaken and launch sites may defect, but the crisis does not begin with an immediate strike.

Special Payload Crisis: Allows countries that already possess special warheads and stockpiles to adapt them for missile delivery. The scenario grants no chemical, biological, nuclear, or thermonuclear weapon by itself.

Retaliation Network: Builds retaliation networks with warning systems and national response postures. Lower intensities avoid an immediate launch, while higher intensities place more pressure on the warning chain.
Type Options: Global Proliferation, Saturation War, Command Breakdown, Special Payload Crisis, Retaliation Network
Intensity Scaling:
§RStarts the Missile Age immediately.§! A limited group receives early missile technology, modest reserves, one launch site, and secure command.

§RStarts the Missile Age immediately.§! More countries receive stronger reserves and secondary launch sites, and missile crises may begin to develop.

§RStarts the Missile Age immediately.§! Most eligible countries receive mature regional programmes, larger reserves, advanced sites, and a greater risk of crisis.

§RStarts the Missile Age immediately.§! Every eligible country receives the strongest supported programme and faces the full range of missile risks. The campaign continues.

Details:
Launch a worldwide crisis led by a wholly fictional jihadist movement. Choose how its networks deploy and how widely the initial wave spreads. Muslim governments and communities remain ordinary targets and determined opponents, never default supporters or recruits.

Dispersed Networks: Seed more active countries and fewer territorial commands across urban, transport, border, and capital contexts. Coordination begins strong while territorial control remains weak.

Border Corridors: Concentrate smaller commands around connected borders, ports, rail routes, and vulnerable neighbors, with stronger external supply and regional war pressure.

Capital Uprisings: Seed high-pressure cells in capitals and administrative centers, opening seizure missions, coup attempts, and short civil wars.

Territorial Fronts: Create larger contiguous territorial commands and conventional wars, immediately opening retaking, blockade, relief, and coalition objectives.

Random Pattern: Select a valid mixture of all four deployment patterns within the chosen intensity, carrier capacity, geographic diversity, and map validity.
Type Options: Dispersed Networks, Border Corridors, Capital Uprisings, Territorial Fronts, Random Pattern
Intensity Scaling:
Low: A limited international crisis begins with a few active countries, one or two small territorial commands, weak coordination, and no immediate Final Jihad.

Medium: Several countries receive active cells, territorial actors, and a connected international network.

High: Large territorial footholds, civil wars, active foreign routes, and coordinated offensives open across several regions.

Maximum: A worldwide crisis begins with widespread cells, multiple territorial fronts, and The Final Jihad active. The False Revelation still requires its normal world-end conditions.

Details:
Launch The Fracture Cascade against the selected share of eligible countries. The scenario creates internal wars without ending the world.

Political Fracture: Prioritizes ideological uprisings, rival legal governments, coalition breakdowns, constitutional disputes, and seizures of central authority.

Independence Cascade: Prioritizes established independence movements, regional secessions, recognition disputes, and wars of separation.

Command Collapse: Prioritizes command schisms, military districts, arsenal seizures, officer disloyalty, and military seizures of central authority.

Universal Fragmentation: Combines political, legal, military, regional, independence, and successor-state crises wherever each form can sustain a conflict.
Type Options: Political Fracture, Independence Cascade, Command Collapse, Universal Fragmentation
Intensity Scaling:
Low: Roughly ten percent of eligible countries face limited uprisings with smaller territorial and military commitments.

Medium: Roughly a quarter of eligible countries face stronger uprisings, established independence movements, and selected multi-front wars.

High: Roughly half of eligible countries face frequent multi-front wars, stronger foreign pressure, and some crises within young successor states.

Maximum: Every eligible country faces its strongest sustainable fracture. Countries outside ordinary human politics remain unaffected, and the scenario does not end the world.
